title: The Pinecone Game
story:
James descended from the heights of Lookout Bridge, leaving the wide view of Oakhaven behind as he followed a winding stone path down into the Terrace Gardens. The morning air was thick and cool, carrying the scent of damp earth and distant woodsmoke—a smell that reminded him of Mateo's warm hearth. He held his green sea-glass to his eye for a moment, watching the world shift into a soft, mossy emerald.

As he walked, James listened to the quiet rhythm of the awakening town. He heard the distant, metallic chime of a clock tower. He heard the gentle rush of a canal lock opening far below. He heard the soft, rapid pitter-patter of four paws trotting over wet leaves.

From behind a clump of wild ferns, a scruffy dog with long, floppy ears and a coat the color of toasted oats bounded into the path. The dog stopped, tilted its head, and let out a soft, inquiring bark. James froze, his hand instinctively reaching for the brass canister at his side. But there was no anger in the dog’s bright eyes, only an immense, trembling curiosity.

The dog trotted closer, dropped a damp pinecone directly at James’s feet, and took two springy steps back, its tail wagging like a rhythmic pendulum. James looked at the pinecone, then at the dog. Slowly, he picked it up and tossed it a short distance. With a joyful yip, the dog scrambled after it, sliding on the wet grass before triumphantly bringing it back.

They played until the sun burned through the morning mist, a small monkey and a scruffy dog sharing a quiet game on the edge of the terraced gardens. When the dog finally sat down, panting happily with its tongue lolling out, it nudged James’s knee with its wet nose. James sat beside his new friend, looking out over the misty valley as the first true warmth of the day began to touch Oakhaven.
